title: media_exchange Module
content_markdown: This module provides the means to exchange media SDP between different SIP proxied calls, and calls started or received from a Media Server. The module itself does not have any media capabilities, it simply exposes primitives to exchange the SDP body between two or more different calls.
overview: This module provides the means to exchange media SDP between different SIP proxied calls, and calls started or received from a Media Server. The module itself does not have any media capabilities, it simply exposes primitives to exchange the SDP body between two or more different calls.
how_it_works:
The module can both originate calls, pushing an existing SDP to a media server, to playback, or simply record an existing RTP, as well as take the SDP of a new call and inject the SDP into an existing, proxied sip call. In order to manipulate the new calls, either generated, or terminated, the module behaves as a back-to-back user agent with the aim of the [OpenSIPS B2B entities module](b2b_entities).

In terms of the SDP media exchanged, the module can have two different modes:

* _Two way Media_ - in this mode, the media of a new call will be pushed towards one of the legs of an existing call. This will result in a party of the call talking with the Media Server. By default, the other participant of the call will be put on hold, but this behavior can be tuned when the new leg is originated.

* _Fork Media_ - the new B2B call, either originated or terminated, will just have a copy of the RTP forked by the media proxy engine. In this mode, the proxied call should have had the RTP relay engaged path before the forked call starts. One can fork only one media leg, or both legs. _NOTE:_ RTPProxy currently does not support stopping media streaming, therefore if the streaming call terminates, RTPProxy will continue streaming, even if there is no one listening on the other end.

This module can provide different functionalities and can be used in various use cases, such as:

* _Call Recording_ - similar to the [OpenSIPS SIPREC](siprec) module, it can be used to fork the RTP media to a new SIP destination, but without the SIPREC payload.

* _Call Listening_ - one might want to call into OpenSIPS and start listening an existing call.

* _Call Announcements_ - inject an announcement from a Media Server to the participants of an ongoing call.

dependencies_required.reason: Dialog module for keeping track of the proxied calls.

dependencies_required.reason: Back-2-Back module used form manipulating calls with the Media Server.

exported_functions.name: media_fork_to_uri

parameters.name: URI
parameters.description: destination where to push the current call's media

parameters.name: leg
parameters.description: the leg that will be streamed. Possible values are caller, callee and both. If missing, the direction of the indialog request is used.

parameters.name: headers
parameters.description: optional headers added to the generated request.

parameters.name: medianum
parameters.description: the media stream that will be forked within the call. First index is 0. If missing, all media streams of that leg(s) are streamed.

parameters.name: instance
parameters.description: a unique name for identifying the forking instance. If missing, the default name is assumed.

exported_functions.description: Behaves as a B2B user agent client to initiate a call to a SIP URI and then stream the media to the SDP received in the 200 OK response. Can be called multiple times, and will create a new call for each invocation. The generated calls can be identified using the _instance_ parameter.

examples.description: Use `media_fork_to_uri()` function to fork media to a Media Server

exported_functions.name: media_fork_from_call

parameters.name: callid
parameters.description: the identifier of the callid to stream/fork media from

parameters.name: leg
parameters.description: the leg that will be streamed. Possible values are caller, callee and both. If missing, both legs will be streamed.

parameters.name: medianum
parameters.description: the media stream that will be forked within the call. First index is 0. If missing, all media streams of that leg(s) are streamed, as long as the body has enough streams. Note: RTPProxy does not do any media mixing, therefore you need to make sure that the INVITE has enough SDP streams to handle all the media streams selected to fork.

parameters.name: instance
parameters.description: a unique name for identifying the forking instance. If missing, the default name is assumed.

exported_functions.description: Starts streaming the media of an existing proxied call, identified by the _callid_ parameter to the SDP in the request's body. Can be called multiple times, and will accept a new call for each invocation. The calls can be identified using the _instance_ parameter.

examples.description: Use `media_fork_from_call()` function to fork all media streams of a call
Use `media_fork_from_call()` function to fork only the first caller's stream

exported_functions.name: media_fork_pause

parameters.name: leg
parameters.description: the leg that will be paused. Possible values are caller, callee and both. If missing, all ongoing media sessions will be paused.

parameters.name: medianum
parameters.description: the media stream to be paused. First index is 0. If missing, all ongoing media streams associated to the selected leg will be paused.

parameters.name: instance
parameters.description: the forking instance to be paused. If missing, all instances are paused.

exported_functions.description: Pauses an existing RTP media streaming session. This function does not terminate the forking call, but only stops sending the RTP. It also re-invites the Media Server to inform about the change.

examples.description: Use `media_fork_pause()` function to temporarily stop the entire media stream of the call

exported_functions.name: media_fork_resume

parameters.name: leg
parameters.default: all existing media legs that are stopped
parameters.description: the leg that will be resumed. Possible values are caller, callee and both. If missing, all existing media legs that are stopped will be started.

parameters.name: medianum
parameters.description: the media stream to be paused. First index is 0. If missing, all ongoing media streams associated to the selected leg will be paused.

parameters.name: instance
parameters.description: the forking instance to be resumed. If missing, all instances are resumed.

exported_functions.description: Resumes the RTP media stream of an existing session/call. This function relies on the fact that a media fork session has been previously started.

examples.description: Use `media_fork_resume()` function to resume a forking previously stopped

exported_functions.name: media_exchange_from_uri

parameters.name: URI
parameters.description: destination used to originate the new call.

parameters.name: leg
parameters.default: module considers it is an hold re-INVITE, and exchanges the media SDP of the other leg
parameters.description: the leg where the new media SDP will be pushed. Possible values are caller and callee. If missing, the module considers it is an hold re-INVITE, and exchanges the media SDP of the other leg.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: custom body used for the generated INVITE. If missing, the body stored in the dialog associated with the involved leg will be used.

parameters.name: headers
parameters.description: optional headers added to the generated request.

parameters.name: nohold
parameters.description: if set to true, the other participant will not be put on hold. This is useful when a new call will be generated for the other leg as well.

exported_functions.description: Originates a call to the specified URI. The SDP in the response is fetched and pushed towards one of the call's legs, resulting in two way audio between the participant of the ongoing call, and the new call. By default, the other participant leg is put on hold. Can be called for an in-dialog request, such as a re-INVITE (for example when putting an entity on hold), or for an INFO request (triggered for example by a DTMF).

examples.description: Use `media_exchange_from_uri()` function to fetch media from a Media Server's call

exported_functions.name: media_exchange_to_call

parameters.name: callid
parameters.description: the identifier of the callid to exchange media.

parameters.name: leg
parameters.description: the leg that will be streamed. Possible values are caller and callee.

parameters.name: nohold
parameters.description: if set to true, the other participant will not be put on hold. This is useful when a new call will be generated for the other leg as well.

exported_functions.description: Pushes the SDP of a new call received in an existing proxied call, resulting in two-way audio between a Media Server that originated the call, and the existing participant of the ongoing proxied call.

examples.description: Use `media_exchange_to_call()` function to make an announcement

exported_functions.name: media_terminate

parameters.name: leg
parameters.description: the leg to terminate the media exchange. Possible values are caller and callee. If missing, the direction of the indialog request is used.

parameters.name: nohold
parameters.description: if set to true, and the other participant is involved in a different media exchange, the current leg is no longer put on hold. Note: if the request that terminates the media exchange is a re-INVITE within the dialog, this function will not un-hold the other leg, as the re-INVITE itself should be relayed further to do that. This behavior can be changed by explicitly setting the nohold parameter

parameters.name: instance
parameters.description: should only be used when terminating a forking instance, and represents the instance to terminate. It must be ommitted when terminating an streaming session. However, for fallback compatibility, if the parameter is missing, and no streaming session is found, the command terminates the default forking instance, if it exists.

exported_functions.description: Terminates an ongoing media session exchange, whether the media is only streamed, or two way audio is flowing. If the participant leg is involved in a different media exchange, the current leg is put on hold.

examples.description: Use `media_terminate()` function to terminate an announcement

exported_functions.name: media_handle_indialog

return_values.condition: indicates that the message has been handled, but there's no additional tasks to be performed in the script.
indicates that there is no ongoing media exchange or fork happening for that call, or that there was no additional logic to do for that request.
indicates that all additional handling of the request was performed, and that the request should not be forwarded to the user agent, but instead it should be dropped.

exported_functions.description: Searches for an existing media session started for any leg, and if there is ongoing session found, it performs additional logic for handling that request. For example, if media has been started in forking mode, and the INVITE is for activating on-hold, then the function will also pause the forked stream. Depending on the return code of this function, one has to perform additional logic in the script.

examples.description: Use `media_terminate()` function to terminate an announcement

exported_mi_functions.name: media_exchange:fork_from_call_to_uri

parameters.name: callid
parameters.description: the callid of the dialog that will have its RTP streamed to the new call towards the Media Server

parameters.name: uri
parameters.description: the destination URI of the new call

parameters.name: leg
parameters.description: indicates the participant leg that will have its RTP streamed in the new call. Possible values are “caller”, “callee” or “both”. If missing, both media streams are forked

parameters.name: headers
parameters.description: extra headers to add to the outgoing request

parameters.name: medianum
parameters.description: the media stream that will be forked within the call. First index is 0. If missing, all media streams of that leg(s) are streamed.

parameters.name: instance
parameters.description: the unique name of the forking instance. If missing, the _default_ name is assumed.

exported_mi_functions.description:
Replaces obsolete MI command: _media\_fork\_from\_call\_to\_uri_.

MI command that has the same behavior as [media\_fork\_to\_uri()](#func_media_fork_to_uri "1.3.1.� media_fork_to_uri(URI[, leg][, headers][, medianum][, instance])"), only that the triggering is not script driven, but exterior driven. Useful for starting listening a call.

examples.code:
# start streaming a callid to record media server
opensips-cli -x mi media\_exchange:fork\_from\_call\_to\_uri \
	callid=c6fdb0f9-47dc-495d-8d38-0f37e836a531 \
	uri=sip:record@127.0.0.1:5080
examples.description: start streaming a callid to record media server

parameters.name: leg

	uri=sip:announcement@127.0.0.1:5080 \

examples.description: start playing back an annoucement to caller

exported_mi_functions.description:
Replaces obsolete MI command: _media\_exchange\_from\_call\_to\_uri\_body_.

MI command that does the same thing as the [media\_exchange:from\_call\_to\_uri](#mi_from_call_to_uri "1.4.2.� media_exchange:from_call_to_uri") MI function, but also allows you to specify a custom body in the outgoing request. The body has to be specified in the mandatory _body_ parameter, all the other parameters being the same as the ones of [media\_exchange:from\_call\_to\_uri](#mi_from_call_to_uri "1.4.2.� media_exchange:from_call_to_uri").

exported_mi_functions.name: media_exchange:terminate

parameters.name: callid
parameters.description: the callid of the dialog that will have the media exchange terminated.

parameters.name: leg
parameters.description: the leg for whom to terminate the media exchange. Accepted values are _caller_, _callee_ and _both_. If missing, all media sessions are terminated.

parameters.name: nohold
parameters.description: if specified and has a non-zero value, the leg that is being terminated is not put on hold if the other participant still has an ongoing media session.

parameters.name: instance
parameters.description: should only be used when terminating a forking instance, and represents the instance to terminate. It must be ommitted when terminating an streaming session. However, for fallback compatibility, if the parameter is missing, and no streaming session is found, the command terminates the _default_ forking instance, if it exists.

exported_mi_functions.description:
Replaces obsolete MI command: _media\_terminate_.

MI command to terminate an ongoing media exchange.

examples.code:
# terminate a caller announcement
opensips-cli -x mi media\_exchange:terminate \
	callid=c6fdb0f9-47dc-495d-8d38-0f37e836a531 \
	leg=caller
